data.title: Why Singapore keeps surfacing in Nvidia chips and China controversy
data.content:
A fifth person was handed 41 charges on Friday in a Singapore fraud case involving computer servers that might have contained Nvidia chips and exported to Malaysia. The alleged transactions in the broader case totaled about $390 million, prosecutors said March last year.

The investigations into several companies and key officials, including Megaspeed International, began in February 2025 and remained ongoing as of Thursday. [...] Experts have pointed to gaps in enforcement of U.S. export restrictions and Singapore's corporate system that make it hard to trace where advanced Nvidia chips ultimately end up.

Nvidia chips can be legally sold to customers in other countries, such as Malaysia or Singapore, and then illicitly resold or re-exported to China. Chinese companies can also legally gain remote access to the most advanced AI chips hosted in data centers outside China rather than buying the hardware directly. [...] Authorities have been examining whether servers exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the domestic market were subsequently rerouted to another destination, contrary to declarations made in Singapore, the Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement late Thursday.

Singapore has faced international scrutiny, particularly from the U.S., over its role as a major billing and potential transit hub for Nvidia chips that U.S. officials say have reached China through Southeast Asia.
